model: Regulated utility FCFE at cost of equity (rate-base reinvestment, engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management's reaffirmed >8% adjusted-EPS CAGR through 2030 (Q3-2026: incremental capital moves ETR 'toward the upper half' of the 2027-2030 outlook ranges), corroborated by the 3-yr and 5-yr book-equity CAGR of 9.2% and by FY2026 guidance midpoint $4.40 vs FY2025 diluted GAAP EPS $3.91 (+12.5%). Base-case NI grows ~11%/yr 2027-2030 = ~8.5% EPS growth after ~2.3%/yr issuance dilution.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 9.2% diverges >30% from revenue 3-yr CAGR of -2.0% and from EPS 3-yr CAGR of 13.8%. Revenue is distorted by fuel pass-through (FY2022 fuel costs $2.8B vs $2.4B FY2025) and the July 2025 sale of the gas distribution business; GAAP EPS is distorted by the FY2022 base ($2.70, Palisades/Indian Point exit charges) and FY2024 impairments ($2.47). Book equity grows through issuance (24.5m new shares in 9M-2026 alone) as well as retention, so equity CAGR overstates per-share compounding. EPS history in the CSV is post the December 2024 2-for-1 split from FY2022 onward; the FY2020 figure ($6.94) is pre-split and has been halved for the 5-yr CAGR. Owner-FCF (FCFE) CAGRs are null because FY2025 FCFE is negative (dividends $1,074m less $1,173m equity issued).

scenario_narratives.base: Entergy delivers the capital plan broadly as guided: $54.8B of 2027-2030 construction (the Meta West Memphis combined-cycle/battery build, the Google campus expansion, Richland Parish, Waterford 5/6, Amite South transmission) enters rate base on time, formula rate plans in Louisiana, Mississippi and Arkansas true up annually without material disallowance, and adjusted EPS compounds at ~8.5% from the $4.40 FY2026 midpoint to ~$6.05 in 2030 while ~$5.2B of equity is issued at a premium to book. Growth then decelerates through 2035 as the plan rolls off and unsigned pipeline is not assumed. The axes are (1) regulatory treatment of large-load generation cost allocation, (2) construction execution on 23 GW of gas plants, and (3) the equity market continuing to fund the plan at ~25x earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 7-12 GW data-centre pipeline converts: a further 5+ GW of hyperscaler contracts are signed in 2027-2028 with minimum-take and credit-support structures the commissions accept, the capital plan extends past 2030 at a similar run-rate, earned ROE holds at the top of the bandwidth, and EPS compounds ~9.5% through 2030 and high single digits to 2035. Equity is issued at premium multiples so dilution stays near 2%/yr. Even here the terminal value is capped at ~15.5x 2035 earnings, so the bull case is about duration of growth, not a re-rating.
scenario_narratives.bear: Concentration and regulation bite together: the LPSC adopts its staff's position that data-centre-driven generation (Cottonwood first) must be borne by those customers, a hyperscaler project is delayed or cancelled after plant is committed, Grand Gulf or River Bend has an extended outage, and a major Gulf hurricane forces securitised storm costs with recovery lag. Credit metrics (FFO/debt) force more equity at lower prices; EPS growth slips to ~5% and the dividend grows 4%. Terminal growth 2.5%. This is a regulated-return business, so the bear case is a slower, more diluted compounder -- not an impairment of the franchise -- which is why its value stays within ~25% of base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ETR is valued as a regulated compounder of book equity: the flow to shareholders is dividends less the equity they must keep putting in, capitalised at a 7.5% cost of equity, with the terminal value held at sector-median earnings multiples. Reported FCF is deeply negative through 2030 by design (a $55B plan funded by debt, hybrids, customer advances and equity) and is not the flow that matters. The model deliberately does not credit shareholders with the cash-tax benefit of bonus depreciation and PTC transfers (they flow to customers through rate base), does not add the $4.2B of pre-funding cash, and does not assume unsigned pipeline. At the current price the market is paying ~25x FY2026 earnings for a utility guiding >8% EPS growth; the required-return table shows the discount rate at which that price is fair -- roughly 6.5% with 3.5% perpetual growth -- which is the real question for a buyer.
key_risks_to_valuation: Large-load cost allocation: LPSC staff has already argued Cottonwood's costs should fall on data-centre customers rather than general ratepayers; a pattern of such rulings would strand or delay recovery on generation built for hyperscalers
Hyperscaler concentration: a Meta or Google campus delay or cancellation after plant is committed leaves ETR seeking recovery from general customers in a low-income territory
Funding execution: $5.2B of equity 2027-2030 plus junior subordinated hybrids and rising interest costs; a wider equity discount or a credit downgrade raises dilution
Gulf Coast hurricanes and winter storms (Fern, January 2026) with securitisation lag; nuclear outage risk at Grand Gulf and River Bend
Rate sensitivity: as a bond proxy the stock's multiple moves with long yields; each 50bp on the cost of equity moves base value ~15%
Terminal assumptions: value is ~80% terminal; the 3.5% perpetual growth and 16.8x implied exit P/E are the two judgments a reader should test first

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 12 stock-based compensation tables, 'Compensation expense included in Entergy's consolidated net income': stock options 4.0 + restricted/performance units 25.9 + 11.4 + 1.8 = $43.1m (ETR_Annual_FY2025.txt:19729, 19822, 19863, 19913). 9M-2026 run-rate $42.0m (Q3-2026 10-Q:8777, 8827) = 0.38% of revenue, used forward. No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed; the amounts are immaterial at 0.3% of revenue.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 477.8m = 607,671,791 issued less 129,850,779 treasury shares at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet, :7615/7619); Q3-2026 diluted weighted average was 474.4m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside net income, and the genuine non-SBC issuance -- the ~$5.2B of equity management expects to issue 2027-2030 ($2.2B already under forward sale agreements) -- is deducted from the flows as part of the equity-reinvestment line, so the count must not be grown as well. The $1.93B issued January-September 2026 (ATM forwards and the May 2026 19.2m-share forward offering, partly settled) is ALREADY in the 477.8m count and is therefore NOT deducted from the Y1 (FY2026) flow; deducting it too would charge the same cash twice. Remaining post-September 2026 settlement is folded into the 2027 issuance figure.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest free cash flow to equity. USD build: 10-year US Treasury ~4.15%, equity beta 0.60 (five-year monthly; ETR is a bond-proxy regulated utility, slightly above Con Edison's 0.55 given parent leverage and the growth-capex programme), ERP 5.5% -> CAPM 7.45%, rounded to 7.5% and applied identically to all three scenarios so that regulatory, construction and large-load-contract risk is charged once, in the flows and the weights, never a second time through the rate. For reference the authorised ROEs in ETR's jurisdictions (9.7% Louisiana FRP, ~9.5-10.5% elsewhere) are regulatory book returns, not market discount rates; ETR's senior unsecured debt costs ~5.5-6%. The sensitivity grid spans 5.5-9.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are left as an operating cost inside pre-tax income; lease liabilities are excluded from the (zero) net-debt bridge since the flow being valued is post-financing. One treatment, consistently. Flag: the October 2026 Waterford 6 build-to-suit arrangement (investors spend up to $1.875B, triple-net lease from ~2029, SOFR-plus lease cost, purchase option) keeps ~$1.9B of generation off balance sheet during construction; its lease cost will sit inside O&M from 2029 and is implicitly inside the net-income path, not modelled as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Subsidiaries' preferred stock ($219m) and non-controlling interests take $15-18m/yr (FY2025 $15.1m, 9M-2026 $16.4m). Absorbed by using a 22.5% engine tax rate against the 21.9% FY2025 book effective rate (0.6pp leakage), so engine NOPAT ties to net income ATTRIBUTABLE to Entergy ($1,758m FY2025), not consolidated net income ($1,773m).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Regulated utility FCFE (free cash flow to equity) capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF component engine -- the folder's precedent for a rate-regulated electric utility is ED (2026-09). Rationale: dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no regulated-utility row; ETR's reported FCF (OCF less construction expenditures) is structurally negative for the whole 2027-2030 capital plan ($54.8B: 17.2/16.4/11.9/9.3B per the Q3-2026 10-Q table at :7153-7159, against D&A of ~$2.1-3.1B) -- FY2025 was -$2.5B and 9M-2026 -$2.8B -- so an unlevered EV-less-net-debt DCF would be >100% terminal value against $34.8B of debt on a $52.8B market cap and would say nothing about the business. A cost-of-service utility is priced on rate-base growth x allowed ROE; the skill's own principle for a post-financing flow is 'capitalise at the cost of equity and never subtract net debt afterwards' (NAB.AX, IAG.AX, ED: net_debt = 0). ENGINE MAPPING (read the sliders with this key): 'revenue' = total operating revenues (FY2025 $12,947m); 'EBITDA margin' = (pre-tax income + D&A + SBC) / revenue, i.e. EBITDA AFTER net interest expense and other income (AFUDC, interest and investment income), NOT operating EBITDA -- FY2025 operating EBITDA margin was 40.8%, the engine's FY2025-equivalent is 33.9% = (2,271 + 2,078 + 43) / 12,947; 'SBC' = 0.38% of revenue; 'D&A' = book depreciation and amortisation (FY2025 $2,078m, 16.0% of revenue; 9M-2026 +5%; projected to grow 8-10%/yr 2027-2030 as ~$55B of plant enters service, 15.3-17.1% of revenue); 'cash tax rate' = 22.5% = the BOOK effective rate (FY2025 21.9%, 9M-2026 21.4%, Q3-2026 22.8%) plus 0.6pp for subsidiary preferred/NCI dividends, because under cost-of-service ratemaking the cash-tax benefit of bonus depreciation and transferable production tax credits accrues to customers through accumulated deferred income taxes as a rate-base offset, not to shareholders -- ETR's cash taxes were a $515m RECEIPT in FY2025 and a $225m receipt in 9M-2026 (PTC transfers) and that benefit is deliberately not projected; so engine EBIT = pre-tax income and NOPAT = net income attributable; 'capex' = D&A + the equity reinvestment required to fund rate-base growth (book-equity growth = NI + SBC + equity issuance - dividends in the plan years 2026-2030, then NI x reinvestment ratio gliding toward g/ROE for 2031-2035), so that engine owner FCF = NI - equity reinvestment = FREE CASH FLOW TO EQUITY = dividends - equity issuance - SBC (SBC is deducted because the count is held flat: the shares issued to employees are notionally repurchased). Working capital 0 (customer advances for construction -- $4.2B at 2026-09-30, largely hyperscaler prepayments -- are pass-through funding of plant that customers, not shareholders, will own the benefit of; they are not modelled as equity value). FY0 = FY2025 actuals: revenue 12,947; pre-tax income 2,271; D&A 2,078; income taxes 498; NI attributable 1,758 (diluted EPS $3.91 on 450.2m); common dividends paid 1,074; equity issued 1,136 common + 37 treasury = 1,173 (10-K cash flow :13738-13748); FCFE = 1,074 - 1,173 - 43 = -142 = last_fcf; reported_fcf = -98.5 is the same flow with SBC added back (it is NOT OCF less capex, which was -$2,534m and is not the flow this model values). Y1 = FY2026: adjusted EPS guidance $4.35-4.45 (narrowed, low end raised, Q3-2026 release 2 Nov 2026) on ~470m diluted weighted shares -> NI ~$2,065m base; dividends ~$1,210m (9M paid $885m + Q4 at the $0.68 declared in October 2026 on 477.8m); issuance deducted 0 (see share_count_basis). Y1 is discounted one full period per house convention although ten months of FY2026 have elapsed; that is conservative by roughly 5% of value (~$4/share) and more than offsets the ~$1.8/share of 9M-2026 dividends already paid that sit inside the Y1 flow. TERMINAL CAP: terminal_cap_multiple 30x terminal FCFE, which at the terminal reinvestment ratios (40% base, 48% bull, 32% bear of NI) equals 16-18x terminal earnings, the regulated-utility sector's long-run median P/E; the tech default 20x FCFE would be ~12x P/E and would bind in every scenario. Base-case Gordon at 7.5%/3.5% is 25.9x FCFE = 16.8x 2035 earnings, so the cap does not bind; it binds only in the bull case (Gordon 29.7x at 4.0%). CASH: $4.2B of cash at 2026-09-30 is pre-funding of the 2027 construction programme (raised through $7.7B of long-term debt and $1.9B of equity in 9M-2026), not surplus; it is not added to equity value. Buybacks: none (Entergy is a net ISSUER; buyback_cash 0; treasury-stock proceeds are employee-plan reissuance). Consolidated book ROE: FY2025 11.0% (1,758 / avg equity 16.1B), above the ~9.7-10.5% authorised utility ROEs because of parent-level leverage; the 2030 base NI of $3,135m on ~$28.6B average book equity is the same 11%, so the plan-year path does not assume earned-ROE expansion. Routing per Step 2: not a REIT (plant at depreciated cost, no IAS 40), not a bank, not a holdco; an operating company whose reported FCF is structurally negative through a capex supercycle, hence the FCFE adaptation rather than the unlevered default.

bear.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m). NI: 2,045 (bottom of FY2026 guidance), then +8%/yr 2027-2030 (2,209 / 2,385 / 2,576 / 2,782; ~4.8% EPS CAGR after heavier dilution -- a clear miss of the >8% target) as the LPSC follows its staff's Cottonwood objections into cost-allocation disallowances on large-load generation, one hyperscaler campus is delayed or cancelled leaving plant to be recovered from general customers, and a major hurricane season adds securitised storm cost with regulatory lag; then 5 / 4.5 / 4 / 3.5 / 3% for 2031-2035. D&A 2,190 -> 2,900 (2030) -> 3,550. Dividends: DPS growing 4%/yr: 1,210 / 1,323 / 1,422 / 1,518 / 1,617. Equity issuance higher as FFO/debt pressure forces more equity at lower prices: 1,900 / 1,800 / 1,500 / 1,300 (2027-2030, $6.5B). Reinvestment 2031-2035 = 68 / 56 / 46 / 39 / 32% of NI (lower growth needs less). FCFE: 1,156 / -634 / -438 / -44 / 252 / 935 / 1,343 / 1,714 / 2,004 / 2,301. Terminal g 2.5%: Gordon 20.5x FCFE = ~14x 2035 earnings.

base.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m). Revenue: FY2026 +10% (9M-2026 +10.9%), then 9/8/7/6% as the Meta/Google-driven generation enters service and large-load volumes ramp, tapering to 3.5%. NI attributable: 2,065 (FY2026 guidance midpoint $4.40 x ~470m), then 2,290 / 2,545 / 2,830 / 3,135 for 2027-2030 (+11%/yr = ~8.5% EPS CAGR after ~2.3%/yr dilution from $5.2B of issuance at $115-140; 2030 EPS ~$6.05), then 7/6/5/4.5/4% for 2031-2035 as the construction plan rolls off. D&A 2,190 -> 3,090 (2030) -> 4,060 (2035). Dividends: DPS $2.60 (2026, $0.68 declared October 2026) growing 6.5%/yr x rising share count: 1,210 / 1,349 / 1,469 / 1,601 / 1,740. Equity issuance: 0 remaining in 2026 (the $1.93B raised to September is already in the count), then 1,700 / 1,600 / 1,100 / 800 for 2027-2030 = the $5.2B management guided, front-loaded with the capex. Equity reinvestment 2031-2035 = 70 / 60 / 50 / 45 / 40% of NI (glide from the plan-year 72% toward g/ROE at an 11% consolidated ROE). FCFE: 1,156 / -410 / -195 / 433 / 868 / 1,006 / 1,422 / 1,866 / 2,146 / 2,434. Terminal g 3.5%: structural load growth (data centres, Gulf South industrial reshoring, electrification) at inflation-plus; Gordon 25.9x FCFE = 16.8x 2035 earnings, below the 30x cap.

bull.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m). NI: 2,090 (top of FY2026 guidance), then +12.5%/yr 2027-2030 (2,351 / 2,645 / 2,976 / 3,348; ~9.5% EPS CAGR -- the top of the outlook ranges), then 10 / 8 / 7 / 6 / 5% for 2031-2035 as a further 5+ GW of the 7-12 GW data-centre pipeline converts to signed contracts and keeps rate-base growth near double digits past the current plan. D&A 2,190 -> 3,250 (2030) -> 4,440. Dividends: DPS growing 7.5%/yr: 1,210 / 1,372 / 1,520 / 1,673 / 1,837. Equity issuance higher with the larger plan: 2,000 / 1,900 / 1,500 / 1,200 (2027-2030, $6.6B), issued at premium prices. Reinvestment 2031-2035 = 78 / 70 / 62 / 55 / 48% of NI. FCFE: 1,156 / -688 / -446 / 101 / 559 / 810 / 1,193 / 1,617 / 2,030 / 2,463. Terminal g 4.0%; Gordon 29.7x FCFE is just under the 30x cap (~15.5x 2035 earnings on a 52% payout).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 30x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the incremental growth now rests on a handful of hyperscaler contracts (Meta, Google) whose cost allocation is being actively contested before the LPSC (Cottonwood staff testimony), on a five-regulator footprint, with Gulf Coast hurricane exposure and a funding plan that needs $5.2B of equity plus hybrids and customer advances. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right -- further pipeline conversion, commission acceptance of the large-load tariffs, on-budget delivery of 23 GW of gas generation, and equity markets absorbing issuance at a premium -- and the terminal value is already capped at sector multiples so upside is duration-limited. Base 50%: contracted agreements, formula rate plans and a narrowed FY2026 guide give good visibility on the central path through 2030.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is not meaningful for ETR: SBC is 0.38% of revenue, so the house/street band is only ~$3.4/share wide (base 77.2 house vs 80.6 street) and the current price sits ~10 band-widths above it. Read the price against the house value and the required_return_table, not the band. The band has effectively collapsed as in an SBC-zero market; it is left as computed rather than nulled because SBC is non-zero.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
